sc: Breastfed toddler, no vitamin D drops, kept indoors, bowed legs, wide wrists → Nutritional rickets
4-month-old with soft skull bones that yield like a ping-pong ball → Craniotabes (early rickets)
Rickets, low phosphate, normal PTH, father affected → X-linked hypophosphataemic rickets
f: Delayed sitting and walking · bone pain, irritability · sweating of the head · late teeth · infant: hypocalcaemic seizures or tetany
Craniotabes, large late fontanelle, frontal bossing · rachitic rosary, Harrison sulcus · wide wrists · bow legs or knock knees
Ca normal/low · phosphate low · ALP high · PTH high · 25(OH)D < 30 nmol/L · wrist X-ray: cupping, fraying, wide growth plate
Vitamin D-dependent rickets · X-linked hypophosphataemia · renal osteodystrophy (CKD, high phosphate) · scurvy
Vitamin D 2000–6000 IU/day × 12 weeks (or single stoss dose) + calcium 500 mg/day · tetany: 10% Ca gluconate 0.5 ml/kg IV
ALP falls · X-ray healing line in 2–4 weeks · not healing → look for non-nutritional rickets
trap: Bow legs appear only after walking; in a young infant look for craniotabes · rickets gives a large fontanelle, never microcephaly · high phosphate points to CKD, not nutritional rickets
